summary.text: A humid continental climate, defined by climatologist Wladimir Köppen in 1900, has four distinct seasons, with warm to hot summers and cold, snowy winters.
To qualify, the coldest month must average below 0 °C or −3 °C, and at least four months must average 10 °C or more.
Those cut-offs were not arbitrary: 10 °C is roughly the lowest average temperature trees need to reproduce and grow.

items.prompt: Humid continental climates are common in North America, Europe and Asia but rare in the Southern Hemisphere. Why?

options.label: Cold winds off Antarctica freeze those latitudes
More ocean and less land there soften the seasons
Southern mountain ranges block the summer heat
Southern summers are too short for four seasons

items.explain: At those latitudes the Southern Hemisphere has more ocean and a smaller land mass, so the sea moderates temperatures.

items.prompt: A city with this climate has fairly dry air in summer. Why can it still be called "humid" continental?

options.label: Humidity is measured only in winter
Melting snow is counted as humidity
It just means it isn't semi-arid or arid
The label comes from nearby big lakes

items.explain: The "humid" designation means only that the climate is not dry enough to be classed as semi-arid or arid.

items.prompt: You're moving to a city with a humid continental climate. Should you expect to shovel your driveway in winter?

options.label: Only if you live high in the mountains
Yes, it falls everywhere with this climate
No, winter there brings mostly cold rain
Only in rare years with a strong monsoon

items.explain: Snowfall isn't part of the definition, but it occurs in all areas with this climate and is almost guaranteed each winter.

items.prompt: Travel toward the pole out of a humid continental zone. What climate do you usually reach next?

options.label: A humid subtropical climate
A dry-summer Mediterranean climate
A mild, rainy oceanic climate
A subarctic climate with conifers

items.explain: Poleward, these climates turn into subarctic climates whose short summers allow only conifer trees.

items.prompt: Humid continental parts of East Asia have much colder winters than similar latitudes elsewhere. What causes this?

options.label: The strong Siberian High
Their high average elevation
A cold current off the coast
Thick monsoon clouds all winter

items.explain: In East Asia the strong Siberian High brings much colder winter temperatures than at similar latitudes around the world.

items.prompt: Köppen required at least four months averaging 10 °C or more for this climate. What was that line meant to capture?

options.label: When lakes stop freezing over each year
The southern edge of lasting winter snow
The warmth wheat needs to ripen fully
Roughly the minimum for trees to grow

items.explain: The 10 °C average was found to be roughly the minimum temperature for tree reproduction and growth; the −3 °C line, by contrast, tracked the edge of winter snowpack.
